evidence.claim: Historian Stanley W. Paher places Conrad Keil, also known as Kyle, in the canyon with a sawmill and cabin circa 1870–1880.
evidence.quote: According to historian Stanley W. Paher, Conrad Keil (a.k.a. Kyle) built a sawmill and cabin in Kyle Canyon circa 1870–1880.

evidence.claim: Edmund W. Griffith established a campground around 1905 and built Charleston Park Lodge around 1915.
evidence.quote: Edmund W. Griffith initially established a campground in Kyle Canyon around 1905

evidence.claim: built Charleston Park Lodge around 1915

evidence.claim: The Civilian Conservation Corps based Camp Charleston Mountain in the canyon beginning in 1933.

evidence.claim: Start with the mountain village, which lies in Kyle Canyon.
evidence.quote: The main town in the area is also named Mount Charleston (Nevada), which lies in Kyle Canyon.

evidence.claim: The Spring Mountains have conifers at their upper elevations, with juniper and pinyon below and creosote bush at their bases.
evidence.quote: The bases of the mountains are part of the Mojave zone dominated by creosote bush and white bursage, then rising to a blackbush scrub zone, followed by a pygmy conifer zone with juniper, pinyon pine, and mountain mahogany, and topped by a montane zone with many species of conifers

evidence.claim: Tule Springs offers a separate Las Vegas excursion to natural spring-fed lakes in the Mojave Desert.
evidence.quote: The park is centered on Tule Springs, a series of small natural spring-fed lakes that form an oasis in this part of the Mojave Desert.

evidence.claim: The village’s approximately 7,500-foot elevation puts it above Las Vegas, at about 2,000 feet.

evidence.claim: Mount Charleston takes its name from the nearby mountain and occupies a valley known for hiking trails.
evidence.quote: The town of Mount Charleston is named for nearby Mount Charleston

evidence.claim: occupies a valley known for hiking trails
evidence.quote: The town of Mount Charleston is in a valley of the Spring Mountains to the northwest of Las Vegas, noted for its hiking trails.

evidence.claim: Its early vacation development included Edmund W. Griffith’s Charleston Park Lodge, later enlarged with a casino and lost to fire in 1961.
evidence.quote: A casino was later added to the lodge, which burned down in 1961.

evidence.claim: The lodge stood in what is now Old Town.
evidence.quote: His development, shown on the 1929 plat map to be in the present day Old Town Subdivision, was named Charleston Park.

evidence.claim: Historical postcards held by the Pomona, California, public library place that lodge at the present location of the Mount Charleston Library and Volunteer Fire Department.
evidence.quote: Historical postcards in the Pomona, Calif. Public Library show that lodge was at the present location of the Mt. Charleston Library and Volunteer Fire Department

evidence.claim: A propeller from a downed aircraft forms part of the Silent Heroes of the Cold War Memorial at Spring Mountains Visitor Gateway.
evidence.quote: It features a propeller from the downed aircraft (which was recovered decades later from the crash site) and a granite monument.

evidence.claim: Installed in 2015, the memorial recalls a 1955 crash near Mount Charleston’s summit.
evidence.quote: The Silent Heroes of the Cold War Memorial was installed at the Spring Mountains Visitor Gateway in 2015.

evidence.claim: The aircraft was traveling from Burbank to Groom Lake for work on the secret U-2 program when it crashed during a blizzard.
evidence.quote: The plane was on route on November 17, 1955, from Burbank (location of Lockheed's Skunkworks), to Groom Lake (Area 51) (then known as Watertown Strip) to work on the secret U-2 plane development.

evidence.claim: All fourteen men aboard died, including military personnel and civilian contractors, engineers and technicians.
evidence.quote: Fourteen men (a mix of military staffers and civilian subcontractors, engineers, and technicians) were on board when it crashed during a blizzard, all of whom died.

evidence.claim: The recovered propeller stands with a granite monument; aircraft wreckage also remains near the summit, just off the southern loop trail.
evidence.quote: There are still remains from the plane that can be hiked to just off the main southern loop trail to the peak.

evidence.claim: The recovered propeller stands with a granite monument
evidence.quote: It features a propeller from the downed aircraft (which was recovered decades later from the crash site) and a granite monument.

evidence.claim: Natural spring-fed lakes form a Mojave Desert oasis within Floyd Lamb Park at Tule Springs.
evidence.quote: The park is centered on Tule Springs, a series of small natural spring-fed lakes that form an oasis in this part of the Mojave Desert.

evidence.claim: The springs also supported a guest ranch for out-of-state residents seeking Nevada divorces.
evidence.quote: More recently, it served as a guest ranch for out-of-state residents seeking to "live" in Nevada and gain access to its easy divorce requirements.

evidence.claim: Most ranch buildings date from the 1940s, when Prosper Jacob Goumond developed the divorce ranch.
evidence.quote: Most of the buildings on the ranch date from the 1940s, when Goumond was developing the Tule Springs Ranch into a "divorce ranch."

evidence.claim: Las Vegas acquired the site as a park in 1964; state control followed in 1977, before the park returned to the city in 2007.
evidence.quote: Tule Springs was first designated as a park when it was acquired by the city of Las Vegas in 1964. It was renamed Floyd Lamb State Park in 1977 when the state assumed control.

evidence.claim: the park returned to the city in 2007
evidence.quote: The park was transferred to the city on July 2, 2007

evidence.claim: Several ranch buildings remain, along with a few peacocks.
evidence.quote: Several of the ranch's buildings remain, as do a few peacocks.

evidence.claim: The ranch became a National Register historic district in 1981.
evidence.quote: The ranch district was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on September 23, 1981.

evidence.claim: The city operates the park.
evidence.quote: Floyd Lamb Park at Tule Springs which is operated by the City of Las Vegas.
